claim: γ-Secretase plays a pivotal role in the central nervous system.
source: γ-Secretase plays a pivotal role in the central nervous system.
evidence: This is a general statement in the abstract that draws from established scientific knowledge about γ-secretase function.

claim: Genetically encoded Förster resonance energy transfer (FRET)-based biosensors enable spatiotemporal recording of γ-secretase activity on a cell-by-cell basis in live neurons in culture.
source: Our recent development of genetically encoded Förster resonance energy transfer (FRET)-based biosensors has enabled the spatiotemporal recording of γ-secretase activity on a cell-by-cell basis in live neurons in culture.
evidence: This claim references the authors' recent development and is supported by citation to their previous work.

claim: The near-infrared (NIR) C99 720–670 biosensor and NIR confocal microscopy can quantitatively record γ-secretase activity in individual neurons in living mouse brains.
source: Here, we employ the near-infrared (NIR) C99 720–670 biosensor and NIR confocal microscopy to quantitatively record γ-secretase activity in individual neurons in living mouse brains.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study, supported by experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: γ-secretase activity may influence the activity of γ-secretase in neighboring neurons in mouse brains.
source: Intriguingly, we uncovered that γ-secretase activity may influence the activity of γ-secretase in neighboring neurons, suggesting a potential 'cell non-autonomous' regulation of γ-secretase in mouse brains.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by correlation analysis data presented in Figures 3, 4, and 5.

claim: γ-secretase is an intramembrane aspartyl protease complex responsible for the proteolytic processing of a wide range of transmembrane proteins.
source: γ-Secretase is an intramembrane aspartyl protease complex responsible for the proteolytic processing of a wide range of transmembrane proteins (Güner and Lichtenthaler, 2020) such as Notch receptors (De Strooper et al., 1998) and APP (De Strooper et al., 1999).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: γ-Secretase processes Notch receptors.
source: γ-Secretase is an intramembrane aspartyl protease complex responsible for the proteolytic processing of a wide range of transmembrane proteins (Güner and Lichtenthaler, 2020) such as Notch receptors (De Strooper et al., 1998) and APP (De Strooper et al., 1999).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to De Strooper et al., 1998.

claim: γ-Secretase processes APP.
source: γ-Secretase is an intramembrane aspartyl protease complex responsible for the proteolytic processing of a wide range of transmembrane proteins (Güner and Lichtenthaler, 2020) such as Notch receptors (De Strooper et al., 1998) and APP (De Strooper et al., 1999).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to De Strooper et al., 1999.

claim: γ-Secretase is ubiquitously expressed in various tissues.
source: γ-Secretase is ubiquitously expressed in various tissues and plays multifunctional roles in essential biology and diseases.
evidence: This is a statement based on established scientific knowledge.

claim: Presenilin (PSEN) 1 and 2 are the catalytic components of γ-secretase.
source: For instance, the mice lacking presenilin (PSEN) 1 and 2, the catalytic component of γ-secretase (Wolfe et al., 1999), are nonviable due to abnormal neurogenesis and vasculature and skeletal formation (Shen et al., 1997; Wong et al., 1997).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Wolfe et al., 1999.

claim: Mice lacking presenilin (PSEN) 1 and 2 are nonviable due to abnormal neurogenesis and vasculature and skeletal formation.
source: For instance, the mice lacking presenilin (PSEN) 1 and 2, the catalytic component of γ-secretase (Wolfe et al., 1999), are nonviable due to abnormal neurogenesis and vasculature and skeletal formation (Shen et al., 1997; Wong et al., 1997).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Shen et al., 1997 and Wong et al., 1997.

claim: Notch knockout (KO) mice recapitulate lethal phenotypes of the PSEN1/2 KO.
source: Notch knockout (KO) mice recapitulate lethal phenotypes of the PSEN1/2 KO (Swiatek et al., 1994; Huppert et al., 2000), suggesting the essential role of γ-secretase-mediated Notch processing in normal development.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Swiatek et al., 1994 and Huppert et al., 2000.

claim: γ-secretase-mediated Notch processing plays an essential role in normal development.
source: Notch knockout (KO) mice recapitulate lethal phenotypes of the PSEN1/2 KO (Swiatek et al., 1994; Huppert et al., 2000), suggesting the essential role of γ-secretase-mediated Notch processing in normal development.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the observation that Notch KO mice recapitulate PSEN1/2 KO phenotypes.

claim: Aberrant Notch processing causes several types of cancer.
source: Aberrant Notch processing also causes several types of cancer (Allenspach et al., 2002; Aster et al., 2017; McCaw et al., 2021) as well as a chronic skin inflammatory disease - Hidradenitis suppurativa (HS) (Wang et al., 2010; Wang et al., 2021).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Allenspach et al., 2002; Aster et al., 2017; McCaw et al., 2021.

claim: Aberrant Notch processing causes Hidradenitis suppurativa (HS).
source: Aberrant Notch processing also causes several types of cancer (Allenspach et al., 2002; Aster et al., 2017; McCaw et al., 2021) as well as a chronic skin inflammatory disease - Hidradenitis suppurativa (HS) (Wang et al., 2010; Wang et al., 2021).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Wang et al., 2010 and Wang et al., 2021.

claim: Conditional knockout of PSEN1 and 2 leads to age-dependent neuronal loss in adult mice.
source: Conditional knockout of PSEN1 and 2 (Saura et al., 2004) or other components of γ-secretase in excitatory (Tabuchi et al., 2009; Acx et al., 2017; Bi et al., 2021), as well as inhibitory neurons (Kang and Shen, 2020), leads to age-dependent neuronal loss in adult mice.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Saura et al., 2004; Tabuchi et al., 2009; Acx et al., 2017; Bi et al., 2021; Kang and Shen, 2020.

claim: Mutations in PSEN genes lead to early-onset familial Alzheimer's disease (AD).
source: Mutations in PSEN genes lead to early-onset familial Alzheimer's disease (AD) (Sherrington et al., 1995; Levy-Lahad et al., 1995) and frontotemporal dementia (FTD) (Raux et al., 2000; Dermaut et al., 2004).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Sherrington et al., 1995 and Levy-Lahad et al., 1995.

claim: Mutations in PSEN genes lead to frontotemporal dementia (FTD).
source: Mutations in PSEN genes lead to early-onset familial Alzheimer's disease (AD) (Sherrington et al., 1995; Levy-Lahad et al., 1995) and frontotemporal dementia (FTD) (Raux et al., 2000; Dermaut et al., 2004).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Raux et al., 2000 and Dermaut et al., 2004.

claim: Some PSEN mutations are linked to epilepsy.
source: Some PSEN mutations are linked to epilepsy (Mann et al., 2001; Velez-Pardo et al., 2004).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Mann et al., 2001 and Velez-Pardo et al., 2004.

claim: γ-Secretase is responsible for the generation of β-amyloid (Aβ) peptides.
source: γ-Secretase is also responsible for the generation of β-amyloid (Aβ) peptides (De Strooper et al., 1999), the accumulation of which in the brain parenchyma is one of the pathological hallmarks of AD.
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to De Strooper et al., 1999.

claim: The accumulation of Aβ peptides in the brain parenchyma is one of the pathological hallmarks of AD.
source: γ-Secretase is also responsible for the generation of β-amyloid (Aβ) peptides (De Strooper et al., 1999), the accumulation of which in the brain parenchyma is one of the pathological hallmarks of AD.
evidence: This is a statement based on established scientific knowledge about AD pathology.

claim: Changes in γ-secretase activity could be linked to the development and progression of neurodegenerative diseases such as AD.
source: Although exactly how is still a matter of debate, it is highly plausible that changes in γ-secretase activity could be ultimately linked to the development and progression of neurodegenerative diseases such as AD.
evidence: This is a speculative statement based on inference from known roles of γ-secretase.

claim: The C99 YPet-mTurquoiseGL (C99 Y-T) biosensor allows recording γ-secretase activity over time, on a cell-by-cell basis, in live neurons in culture.
source: Our recent development of the genetically encoded C99 YPet-mTurquoiseGL (C99 Y-T) biosensor has, for the first time, allowed recording γ-secretase activity over time, on a cell-by-cell basis, in live neurons in culture.
evidence: This claim references the authors' previous work and is supported by citation.

claim: γ-secretase activity is heterogeneously regulated among mouse cortex primary neurons.
source: Using the C99 Y-T biosensor, we uncovered that γ-secretase activity is heterogeneously regulated among mouse cortex primary neurons (Maesako et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Maesako et al., 2020.

claim: Conventional γ-secretase activity assays use APP or Notch1-based recombinant substrates and isolated γ-secretase-rich membrane fractions from rodent/human brains incubated in vitro.
source: In the conventional γ-secretase activity assay, APP or Notch1-based recombinant substrates and isolated γ-secretase-rich membrane fractions from rodent/human brains are incubated in vitro, followed by the detection of either Aβ peptides or the intracellular domain fragment (Hoke et al., 2005; Kakuda et al., 2006; Szaruga et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Hoke et al., 2005; Kakuda et al., 2006; Szaruga et al., 2015.

claim: Conventional γ-secretase activity assays only report γ-secretase activity in a bulk population of cells ex vivo and do not provide spatiotemporal or cell-by-cell information.
source: Although the assay is highly sensitive, it only reports γ-secretase activity in a bulk population of cells ex vivo, and neither provides spatiotemporal nor cell-by-cell information about γ-secretase activity in live cells in vivo.
evidence: This is an inference based on the limitations of conventional assays as described.

claim: The NIR spectral region exhibits greater depth penetration and minimal absorption.
source: To overcome these shortcomings and fulfill the detection capability of γ-secretase activity in vivo, we have recently developed a near-infrared (NIR) analog: C99 720–670 biosensor (Houser et al., 2020), since the NIR spectral region exhibits greater depth penetration and minimal absorption, and this spectral region exhibits low autofluorescence.
evidence: This is a statement based on established knowledge about NIR imaging properties.

claim: The NIR spectral region exhibits low autofluorescence.
source: To overcome these shortcomings and fulfill the detection capability of γ-secretase activity in vivo, we have recently developed a near-infrared (NIR) analog: C99 720–670 biosensor (Houser et al., 2020), since the NIR spectral region exhibits greater depth penetration and minimal absorption, and this spectral region exhibits low autofluorescence.
evidence: This is a statement based on established knowledge about NIR imaging properties.

claim: The C99 720–670 biosensor was developed as a near-infrared (NIR) analog for detecting γ-secretase activity.
source: To overcome these shortcomings and fulfill the detection capability of γ-secretase activity in vivo, we have recently developed a near-infrared (NIR) analog: C99 720–670 biosensor (Houser et al., 2020), since the NIR spectral region exhibits greater depth penetration and minimal absorption, and this spectral region exhibits low autofluorescence.
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Houser et al., 2020.

claim: This study reports the first successful recording of γ-secretase activity on a cell-by-cell basis in live neurons in vivo.
source: This study, for the first time, reports successful recording of γ-secretase activity on a cell-by-cell basis in live neurons in vivo, as opposed to an existing assay in a bulk population of cells ex vivo.
evidence: This is a primary claim of the study supported by the experimental data presented.

claim: NIR confocal microscopy is feasible for monitoring biological events in live mouse brains.
source: Moreover, it highlights the feasibility of NIR confocal microscopy for monitoring biological events in live mouse brains.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the successful application of NIR confocal microscopy in this study.

claim: γ-secretase activity is differently regulated in individual neurons in live mouse brains in vivo.
source: In agreement with the previous study in vitro (Maesako et al., 2020), we uncovered that γ-secretase activity is differently regulated in individual neurons in live mouse brains in vivo.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data and consistent with previous in vitro findings.

claim: There is a statistically significant correlation between γ-secretase activity within a neuron and the activity of γ-secretase in neighboring neurons.
source: Although the effect size is modest, we also found a statistically significant correlation between γ-secretase activity within a neuron and the activity of γ-secretase in neighboring neurons, suggesting a potential 'cell non-autonomous' regulation of γ-secretase activity in mouse brains.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by statistical analysis of experimental data shown in Figures 3 and 4.

claim: The C-terminus of APP C99 is fused to FRET donor and acceptor fluorescent proteins with a flexible linker in the biosensor design.
source: The principle of the biosensors is that the C-terminus of APP C99, an immediate substrate of γ-secretase, is fused to FRET donor and acceptor fluorescent proteins with a flexible linker, and the sensing domains are stabilized near the membrane by connecting to a membrane-anchoring domain.
evidence: This describes the design principle of the biosensor.

claim: The proteolytic processing of C99 within the biosensor by endogenous γ-secretase results in a change in FRET efficiency.
source: The proteolytic processing of C99 within the biosensor by endogenous γ-secretase results in a change in the proximity and/or orientation between the donor and acceptor fluorophores, which can be recorded as altered FRET efficiency (Figure 1A).
evidence: This describes the mechanism of the biosensor and is illustrated in Figure 1A.

claim: The fusion of donor/acceptor fluorescent proteins and the anchor domain does not significantly affect the cleavage efficiency of C99 by γ-secretase.
source: Of note, we ensured that the fusion of the donor/acceptor fluorescent proteins and the anchor domain does not significantly affect the cleavage efficiency of C99 by γ-secretase, which was evaluated by comparing the processing efficiency between the cells expressing C99 FLAG and FRET sensor (Maesako et al., 2020; Houser et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous validation studies.

claim: AAV particles packaging the C99 720–670 biosensor were administered into the somatosensory cortex of 4–6 months old C57BL/6 mice.
source: To elucidate the cell-by-cell regulation of γ-secretase activity in live mouse brains in vivo, we administrated AAV particles packaging the C99 720–670 biosensor under human synapsin promoter into the somatosensory cortex of 4–6 months old C57BL/6 mice implanted with cranial window for imaging (Figure 1B).
evidence: This describes the experimental method used in the study.

claim: Neurons expressing the C99 720–670 sensor were successfully detected 3–4 weeks post AAV injection using confocal microscopy with single-photon excitation at 640 nm wavelength.
source: 3–4 weeks post AAV injection, we successfully detected the neurons expressing the C99 720–670 sensor using a confocal microscope with single-photon excitation at 640 nm wavelength and emission at 700–800 nm range (Figure 1C and D).
evidence: This is an experimental result shown in Figures 1C and D.

claim: The fluorescence signal from the C99 720–670 biosensor could be detected from the brain surface to approximately 100 μm depth.
source: Notably, the fluorescence signal from the C99 720–670 biosensor could be detected from the brain surface to approximately 100 μm depth (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is an experimental observation shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: Approximately 40% of NeuN-positive neurons express the C99 720–670 biosensor.
source: Furthermore, immunohistochemical analysis revealed that approximately 40% of NeuN-positive neurons express the C99 720–670 biosensor (Figure 1—figure supplement 2A and B), and almost all of the C99 720–670 expressing cells are NeuN-positive but GFAP or Iba-1-negative (Figure 1—figure supplement 2A and C).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from immunohistochemical analysis shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: Almost all of the C99 720–670 expressing cells are NeuN-positive but GFAP or Iba-1-negative.
source: Furthermore, immunohistochemical analysis revealed that approximately 40% of NeuN-positive neurons express the C99 720–670 biosensor (Figure 1—figure supplement 2A and B), and almost all of the C99 720–670 expressing cells are NeuN-positive but GFAP or Iba-1-negative (Figure 1—figure supplement 2A and C).
evidence: This is a result from immunohistochemical analysis shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: The C99 720–670 sensor is expressed in neurons.
source: These results suggest that, whereas not all neurons express the C99 720–670 biosensor as expected, the C99 720–670 sensor is expressed in neurons.
evidence: This is a conclusion inferred from the immunohistochemical data showing NeuN-positive, GFAP-negative, and Iba-1-negative staining.

claim: Background fluorescence was subtracted and noise was reduced in the images using median filtering for automatic segmentation of individual neurons.
source: In image processing (Figure 2A), the background fluorescence was first subtracted, and the noise was reduced in the images using median filtering to perform the automatic segmentation of individual neurons.
evidence: This describes the image processing methodology used in the study.

claim: An initial set of ROIs was automatically created on all cellular structures using 3D iterative thresholding.
source: Then, an initial set of ROIs was automatically created on all cellular structures (i.e. cell bodies) in the images using 3D iterative thresholding.
evidence: This describes the image processing methodology used in the study.

claim: ROIs contained non-specific autofluorescent objects whose size and morphology clearly differed from neurons.
source: Of note, we uncovered that those ROIs contained non-specific autofluorescent objects whose size and morphology clearly differed from neurons (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is an observation from the image analysis shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Autofluorescent objects have a significantly lower 720/670 ratio compared to neurons expressing C99 720–670.
source: Moreover, we analyzed the scatter plot of 720/670 ratios (Y-axis: miRFP670 emission, X-axis: miRFP720 emission) and found that the autofluorescent objects have a significantly lower 720/670 ratio compared to neurons expressing C99 720–670 (Figure 2—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is a quantitative observation from scatter plot analysis shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1B.

claim: ROIs exhibiting 720/670 ratios below 1.5 were excluded from the analysis as non-specific objects.
source: Therefore, in the segmentation procedure, we excluded the ROIs exhibiting 720/670 ratios below a set threshold value as 1.5.
evidence: This describes a methodological decision based on the observation of autofluorescent objects.

claim: DAPT dose-dependently increased APP C-terminal fragments (APP CTFs) in mouse brains.
source: We found that DAPT dose-dependently increased APP C-terminal fragments (APP CTFs), immediate substrates of γ-secretase. In contrast, full-length APP levels were not significantly altered (Figure 2—figure supplement 2A), evidencing the inhibition of endogenous γ-secretase in the brain by DAPT.
evidence: This is an experimental result shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2A.

claim: Full-length APP levels were not significantly altered by DAPT administration.
source: We found that DAPT dose-dependently increased APP C-terminal fragments (APP CTFs), immediate substrates of γ-secretase. In contrast, full-length APP levels were not significantly altered (Figure 2—figure supplement 2A), evidencing the inhibition of endogenous γ-secretase in the brain by DAPT.
evidence: This is an experimental result shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2A.

claim: DAPT inhibits endogenous γ-secretase in the brain.
source: We found that DAPT dose-dependently increased APP C-terminal fragments (APP CTFs), immediate substrates of γ-secretase. In contrast, full-length APP levels were not significantly altered (Figure 2—figure supplement 2A), evidencing the inhibition of endogenous γ-secretase in the brain by DAPT.
evidence: This is a conclusion inferred from the accumulation of APP CTFs upon DAPT treatment.

claim: DAPT significantly decreases 720/670 ratios in mouse brains in vivo (22.1% difference between pre- and post-DAPT administration).
source: Whereas we previously found that 720/670 ratios are significantly increased by DAPT in various cell types such as CHO cells and mouse cortical primary neurons (Houser et al., 2020; Maesako et al., 2022), we found that of DAPT significantly decreases 720/670 ratios in mouse brains in vivo (22.1% difference between pre- and post-DAPT administration; Figure 2—figure supplement 2B and C).
evidence: This is an experimental result shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2B and C.

claim: FRET efficiency depends on the proximity and orientation of donor and acceptor fluorescent proteins.
source: FRET efficiency generally depends on the proximity and orientation of donor and acceptor fluorescent proteins, and our new finding suggests that orientation plays a significant role in our γ-secretase FRET biosensor.
evidence: This is a statement based on established knowledge about FRET.

claim: Orientation plays a significant role in the γ-secretase FRET biosensor.
source: FRET efficiency generally depends on the proximity and orientation of donor and acceptor fluorescent proteins, and our new finding suggests that orientation plays a significant role in our γ-secretase FRET biosensor.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the observation that DAPT decreases rather than increases 720/670 ratios in vivo.

claim: Whether the FRET ratio is increased or decreased by γ-secretase-mediated biosensor cleavage depends on cell types.
source: Whether the FRET ratio is increased or decreased by the γ-secretase-mediated biosensor cleavage appears to be dependend on cell types, and therefore must be validated on a model-by-model basis.
evidence: This is a conclusion inferred from the different FRET responses observed in different experimental systems.

claim: Neighboring neurons likely exhibited similar 720/670 ratios (i.e., 'clustering' of neurons displaying similar 720/670 ratios).
source: Intriguingly, we found that neighboring neurons likely exhibited similar 720/670 ratios (i.e. 'clustering' of the neurons displaying similar 720/670 ratios) (Figure 3A).
evidence: This is an observation from the pseudo-color FRET images shown in Figure 3A.

claim: There is a significant linear correlation between the 720/670 ratio in each neuron and the average ratio in five neighboring neurons.
source: Indeed, while the effect is modest, unbiased quantification and statistical analysis showed a significant linear correlation between the 720/670 ratio in each neuron and the average ratio in five neighboring neurons (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is a statistical result from correlation analysis shown in Figure 3B.

claim: A statistically significant positive correlation between the 720/670 ratio in each neuron and the average ratio in five neighboring neurons was detected in three independent mice.
source: Such a statistically significant positive correlation was also detected in two different mice (Figure 3C and D).
evidence: This is a statistical result from correlation analysis shown in Figures 3B, C, and D across three mice.

claim: The C99 720–670 biosensor expression positively correlates with expression in five neighboring neurons.
source: We found that the C99 720–670 biosensor expression, as measured by miRFP670 emission, positively correlates with those in five neighboring neurons (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A), indicating that the AAV was unevenly transduced.
evidence: This is a result from correlation analysis shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1A.

claim: The AAV was unevenly transduced.
source: We found that the C99 720–670 biosensor expression, as measured by miRFP670 emission, positively correlates with those in five neighboring neurons (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A), indicating that the AAV was unevenly transduced.
evidence: This is a conclusion inferred from the correlation of biosensor expression levels in neighboring neurons.

claim: The 720/670 ratio (γ-secretase activity) is not correlated with miRFP670 fluorescence intensity (C99 720–670 biosensor expression).
source: However, the 720/670 ratio (i.e. γ-secretase activity) is not correlated with miRFP670 fluorescence intensity (i.e. C99 720–670 biosensor expression) (Figure 3—figure supplement 1B), suggesting that, while C99 720–670 biosensor expression was not evenly distributed in the brain, such sensor expression pattern did not impact the capability of γ-secretase recording.
evidence: This is a result from correlation analysis shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1B.

claim: The uneven biosensor expression pattern did not impact the capability of γ-secretase recording.
source: However, the 720/670 ratio (i.e. γ-secretase activity) is not correlated with miRFP670 fluorescence intensity (i.e. C99 720–670 biosensor expression) (Figure 3—figure supplement 1B), suggesting that, while C99 720–670 biosensor expression was not evenly distributed in the brain, such sensor expression pattern did not impact the capability of γ-secretase recording.
evidence: This is a conclusion inferred from the lack of correlation between biosensor expression and 720/670 ratio.

claim: The 720/670 ratio was positively correlated with the average 720/670 ratio of the two and ten neighboring neurons.
source: We also ensured that the 720/670 ratio was positively correlated with the average 720/670 ratio of the two and ten neighboring neurons (Figure 3—figure supplement 2A–C).
evidence: This is a result from correlation analysis shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2.

claim: There is a significant linear correlation between the 720/670 ratio in each neuron and the average ratio of neurons within 20 μm radius in three independent mice.
source: We found a significant linear correlation between the 720/670 ratio in each neuron and the average ratio of neurons within 20 μm radius in three independent mice (Figure 4B–D), further evidencing neurons displaying similar 720/670 ratios co-localize in mouse brains.
evidence: This is a statistical result from correlation analysis shown in Figures 4B-D.

claim: Neurons displaying similar 720/670 ratios co-localize in mouse brains.
source: We found a significant linear correlation between the 720/670 ratio in each neuron and the average ratio of neurons within 20 μm radius in three independent mice (Figure 4B–D), further evidencing neurons displaying similar 720/670 ratios co-localize in mouse brains.
evidence: This is a conclusion inferred from the correlation analysis results.

claim: There was no significant correlation between the 720/670 ratio in each neuron and the average ratio of neighboring neurons in DAPT-administered mice.
source: Notably, there was no significant correlation in DAPT-administrated mice (Figure 5A–D), suggesting that the positive correlation between the 720/670 ratio in each neuron and the average ratio in neighboring neurons is canceled by the inhibition of γ-secretase and thus the positive correlation is dependent on γ-secretase activity.
evidence: This is a statistical result from correlation analysis shown in Figure 5.

claim: The positive correlation between the 720/670 ratio in each neuron and the average ratio in neighboring neurons is canceled by the inhibition of γ-secretase.
source: Notably, there was no significant correlation in DAPT-administrated mice (Figure 5A–D), suggesting that the positive correlation between the 720/670 ratio in each neuron and the average ratio in neighboring neurons is canceled by the inhibition of γ-secretase and thus the positive correlation is dependent on γ-secretase activity.
evidence: This is a conclusion inferred from the loss of correlation after DAPT treatment.

claim: The positive correlation between neuronal γ-secretase activities is dependent on γ-secretase activity.
source: Notably, there was no significant correlation in DAPT-administrated mice (Figure 5A–D), suggesting that the positive correlation between the 720/670 ratio in each neuron and the average ratio in neighboring neurons is canceled by the inhibition of γ-secretase and thus the positive correlation is dependent on γ-secretase activity.
evidence: This is a conclusion inferred from the loss of correlation after γ-secretase inhibition.

claim: γ-secretase activities are synchronized in neighboring neurons.
source: Collectively, these results strongly indicate that γ-secretase activities are synchronized in neighboring neurons, and γ-secretase activity may be 'cell non-autonomously' regulated in living mouse brains.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the correlation analyses and DAPT experiments.

claim: γ-secretase activity may be 'cell non-autonomously' regulated in living mouse brains.
source: Collectively, these results strongly indicate that γ-secretase activities are synchronized in neighboring neurons, and γ-secretase activity may be 'cell non-autonomously' regulated in living mouse brains.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the correlation analyses and DAPT experiments.

claim: Individual neurons generate and secrete different levels of Aβ peptides.
source: A previous study employing microengraving technology reported that individual neurons generate and secrete different levels of Aβ peptides (Liao et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Liao et al., 2016.

claim: There are two isoforms of PSEN (PSEN1 and PSEN2) in rodents.
source: Given that there are two isoforms of PSEN (i.e., PSEN1 and PSEN2) and three Aph1 (Aph1a, Aph1b, and Aph1c) in rodents, six different γ-secretase complexes can be expressed by the same cells.
evidence: This is a statement based on established knowledge about PSEN isoforms.

claim: There are three Aph1 isoforms (Aph1a, Aph1b, and Aph1c) in rodents.
source: Given that there are two isoforms of PSEN (i.e., PSEN1 and PSEN2) and three Aph1 (Aph1a, Aph1b, and Aph1c) in rodents, six different γ-secretase complexes can be expressed by the same cells.
evidence: This is a statement based on established knowledge about Aph1 isoforms.

claim: Six different γ-secretase complexes can be expressed by the same cells in rodents.
source: Given that there are two isoforms of PSEN (i.e., PSEN1 and PSEN2) and three Aph1 (Aph1a, Aph1b, and Aph1c) in rodents, six different γ-secretase complexes can be expressed by the same cells.
evidence: This is an inference based on the combinatorial possibilities of PSEN and Aph1 isoforms.

claim: PSEN1 knockout mice displayed a lethal phenotype.
source: While the PSEN1 knockout mice displayed a lethal phenotype (Shen et al., 1997; Wong et al., 1997), the PSEN2 knockout revealed no severe phenotypes (Herreman et al., 1999).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Shen et al., 1997 and Wong et al., 1997.

claim: PSEN2 knockout mice revealed no severe phenotypes.
source: While the PSEN1 knockout mice displayed a lethal phenotype (Shen et al., 1997; Wong et al., 1997), the PSEN2 knockout revealed no severe phenotypes (Herreman et al., 1999).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Herreman et al., 1999.

claim: Aph1a knockout mice show a lethal phenotype.
source: Furthermore, Aph1a knockout mice show a lethal phenotype, whereas those lacking Aph1b or Aph1c survive into adulthood (Serneels et al., 2005).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Serneels et al., 2005.

claim: Mice lacking Aph1b or Aph1c survive into adulthood.
source: Furthermore, Aph1a knockout mice show a lethal phenotype, whereas those lacking Aph1b or Aph1c survive into adulthood (Serneels et al., 2005).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Serneels et al., 2005.

claim: Different γ-secretase complexes exhibit distinct γ-secretase activity.
source: These studies suggest that different γ-secretase complexes exhibit distinct γ-secretase activity.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the different phenotypes of knockout mice for different γ-secretase components.

claim: The spatiotemporal expression of different γ-secretase complexes could explain the cell-by-cell basis heterogeneity in γ-secretase activity.
source: In this sense, the spatiotemporal expression of different γ-secretase complexes could explain the cell-by-cell basis heterogeneity in γ-secretase activity.
evidence: This is a speculative explanation for the observed heterogeneity.

claim: Only a small portion of PSEN might be engaged in the active γ-secretase complex.
source: On the other hand, previous studies utilizing pharmacological agents that bind to the active form of γ-secretase demonstrated that only a small portion of PSEN might be engaged in the active γ-secretase complex (Lai et al., 2003; Placanica et al., 2009).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Lai et al., 2003 and Placanica et al., 2009.

claim: Different equilibrium between the active and inactive γ-secretase could explain the heterogeneity in cellular γ-secretase activity.
source: If this is the case, different equilibrium between the active and inactive γ-secretase could be another possible explanation of the heterogeneity in cellular γ-secretase activity.
evidence: This is a speculative explanation for the observed heterogeneity.

claim: Aβ42 exerts product feedback inhibition on γ-secretase.
source: Interestingly, a recent study shows that Aβ42 exerts product feedback inhibition on γ-secretase (Zoltowska et al., 2024), suggesting that secreted Aβ42 may be one of the negative regulators of γ-secretase.
